issues.body:
The record now correctly re-folds touched groups through the engine path, but both aggregate rules depend on member order and neither says how IVM obtains it. For SUM/AVG: "re-folded in the engine's deterministic member order". For MIN/MAX: "plus enough stable member-order information to reproduce full evaluation".

In full evaluation that order is not a property of the group's membership, it is the row order of the plan output. crates/sparq-engine/src/exec.rs:9463 build_groups collects members as row INDICES into the input Bindings in first-seen order, and group_aggregate (exec.rs:9526) folds each group over those indices; sum_values then folds left from Num::Int(0). So the order is a function of scan/join execution over the current generation, which an incrementally maintained counted relation does not reproduce: CDC arrival order is not index scan order, and a delete-then-reinsert of the same quad can move a member's position.

Two observable consequences, both of which the record itself declares must match exactly: xsd:double SUM/AVG differ in the low bits under a different fold order (f64 addition is non-associative), and MIN/MAX tie-breaking is order-sensitive — minmax_values uses min_by (keeps the FIRST of equal members) and max_by (keeps the LAST), so for numerically equal but lexically distinct members the REPRESENTATIVE TERM is chosen by position, exactly the case the corpus lists. The temporal fast path replicates the same tie rule (see the minmax_temporal doc comment at exec.rs:9920).

This is a specification gap, not a stated-wrong algorithm, and the mandated differential corpus covers both cases, so it is minor rather than a blocker — but as written an implementer can satisfy the letter of the record and still diverge silently.
issues.fix_hint: Say what the stable order key IS, or narrow eligibility. Concretely, either: (a) define the member order as a derived sort key the IVM state can compute without running the plan — e.g. the tuple of contributing leaf-quad ids in the plan's fixed left-deep leaf order — and state that the IvmPlan pins that key so the fold order is a function of current membership rather than of CDC history; or (b) declare that where the plan's row order cannot be reconstructed, the affected group is ineligible: xsd:double SUM/AVG groups and MIN/MAX groups containing two or more members that compare Equal but are not the same RDF term fall back to reevaluate mode, with a fallback-table row for each. Either way, add one sentence stating explicitly that member order is the plan's output row order (exec.rs build_groups collects row indices in first-seen order), so the obligation is not mistaken for insertion order.
issues.title: Aggregate member ORDER is asserted reproducible but no mechanism is specified; it is the plan's row order, which a counted multiset does not carry

issues.body:
The eligible fragment admits "FILTER over variables bound by the BGP, using deterministic scalar expressions ... Boolean connectives, comparisons, arithmetic, bound checks, and deterministic string/numeric functions", and the ineligible list names only "nondeterministic functions such as random, UUID, or current-time evaluation".

sparq lets an embedder register arbitrary extension functions: crates/sparq-engine/src/lib.rs:354 FunctionRegistry::register takes any `Fn(&[Term]) -> Result<Term, String> + Send + Sync`, dispatched through Function::Custom (exec.rs:5893, 5918) and made visible to worker threads via functions::snapshot/worker_install. Such a function may read a clock, a counter, or external state, and its purity is not knowable to the classifier.

The classifier's stated safety net is "an unknown algebra or expression variant is ineligible", but Function::Custom is a KNOWN variant, so the net does not catch this: a FILTER calling a registered extension function reads as an ordinary deterministic function call and would be admitted. Since IVM only ever re-evaluates the filter on changed tuples, an impure filter yields answers that never converge to full evaluation, and the divergence is invisible to a differential test suite that does not register an impure function.
issues.fix_hint: Add Function::Custom / registered extension functions (and, on the aggregate side, AggregateFunction::Custom, already excluded as "custom aggregates") to the ineligible list by name, and state that eligibility is decided over an explicit ALLOW-LIST of engine builtins rather than a deny-list of known-bad ones — that is what makes the classifier genuinely fail-closed. If a purity opt-in is wanted later, note it as future work (e.g. a registry flag marking a function pure) rather than admitting custom calls by default. Consider adding a corpus case that registers a deliberately impure extension function and asserts the subscription selects reevaluate mode.
issues.title: FILTER eligibility does not exclude user-registered extension functions, which are arbitrary host code and a known (not unknown) expression variant

issues.body:
In "The following are eligible", the sentences "Eligibility is provisional until bootstrap has inspected the initial result: a projected result containing a blank node falls back to `reevaluate` mode. If a later commit first produces such a result, the subscription rebuilds and switches to `reevaluate` before emitting that commit's delta." sit inside the `GROUP BY` bullet.

The rule is global — it applies to any projected result, aggregate or not — and the failure table and verification boundary treat it that way. As placed, a reader implementing the classifier could scope the check to grouped queries and leave plain BGP+projection subscriptions exposed to the exact relabeling divergence documented at crates/sparq-server/src/subscriptions.rs:44.
issues.fix_hint: Promote those two sentences out of the GROUP BY bullet into their own paragraph after the eligible list (or into a short "Provisional eligibility" note), making clear the blank-node check applies to every eligible query shape.
issues.title: Blank-node eligibility fallback is nested inside the GROUP BY bullet, reading as aggregate-only

issues.body: The wire-contract JSON example shows a v2 notification with `commitSequence`, but the following paragraph says that in `reevaluate` mode a notification "includes `fromCommitSequence` and `throughCommitSequence` instead of claiming a single source commit". The single example therefore does not show the shape a `reevaluate` subscription actually receives, and does not say whether `commitSequence` is absent or null in that mode — a client-side deserialiser (and the WS/SSE parity tests the record mandates) needs that pinned.
issues.fix_hint: Add a second short JSON block showing a `mode: "reevaluate"` notification with `fromCommitSequence`/`throughCommitSequence`, and state explicitly that `commitSequence` is OMITTED (not null) in that mode and that the two range fields are omitted in `ivm` mode.
issues.title: v2 notification schema example omits the reevaluate-mode fields it later requires

verdict.summary: Docs-only design record for standing-query IVM. All four round-2 majors and both minors are substantively closed, each fix verified against the tree. (1) SUM/AVG drop the add/subtract accumulator: a counted member sequence including errored/non-numeric members is re-folded through the engine's own sum_values + canonicalisation, citing promotion, float order, overflow and error recovery, with recompute-on-touch universal rather than double-only — matching exec.rs:9881, an order-dependent left fold from Num::Int(0) returning None on any non-numeric member. (2) MIN/MAX are derived by minmax_values rather than the head of one ordered index, naming both comparison regimes, the temporal fast path and tie behaviour (exec.rs:9895 + minmax_temporal), with representative-TERM equality as the acceptance criterion. (3) The change-stream dependency is now declared (hard Cargo-feature dep + configured directory), with a fallback-table row and the v2 consequence (reevaluate, no historyCursor), matching the double opt-in in streams.rs. (4) Blank nodes get bootstrap-time and first-occurrence fallbacks, two table rows and a corpus entry, and are excluded from the string-key oracle — the right answer to the relabeling limitation at subscriptions.rs:44. (5) The multi-way delta join is an explicit left-deep recurrence with every ^old operand pinned pre-commit and no stage advanced until the commit is fully computed, closing the double-counting reading. (6) History binds subscription_key to the authenticated principal, defers to the in-server Solid authz surface, and adds unsubscribe purge, key-erasure participation and a finite retention bound. Two minor under-specifications remain, both covered by the mandated corpus: aggregate member ORDER is asserted reproducible with no mechanism (it is the plan's row order — build_groups, exec.rs:9463), and FILTER eligibility does not exclude user-registered extension functions (lib.rs:354), a known variant that slips past the fail-closed net.
